standard_prerequisites.name: The locally finite I-adic filtration and the replacement of a class by its graded pieces
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-from-chow-to-K, invoked at proof lines 4071 and 4083
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the shape of the argument: the descending filtration by powers of the ideal sheaf is locally finite, so the direct sums of the F^p and of the graded pieces are coherent and the class of a module may be replaced by the class of its graded pieces. The proof here re-runs that argument inside the subcategory supported on Z and then goes on to construct the inverse map and prove its additivity, which the cited lemma does not do.

core_obligations: Show the map is surjective: for F in Coh_Z(X) use the descending filtration F^p = I^p F by powers of the ideal sheaf I of Z, argue as in the cited lemma that it is locally finite so that the direct sums of the F^p and of the graded pieces are coherent and supported on Z, replace [F] by the class of the graded pieces, and observe that the direct sum is annihilated by I, hence comes from Coh(Z) (proof lines 4062-4086).

Construct the inverse explicitly by F mapping to the class of the direct sum of F^p/F^{p+1}, and reduce the verification to additivity on short exact sequences 0 -> F -> G -> H -> 0 in Coh_Z(X) (proof lines 4086-4099).

Prove additivity: write for every q the short exact sequence (F intersect I^q G)/(F intersect I^{q+1} G) -> G^q/G^{q+1} -> H^q/H^{q+1} -> 0, introduce the double filtration F^{p,q} = I^p F intersect I^q G, verify with the same local finiteness argument that the class of the graded pieces of F equals both the class of the double graded pieces and the class of the pieces of F as a submodule of G, and combine with the exact sequences to conclude c(G) = c(F) + c(H) (proof lines 4100-4125).
proof_roadmap: Use the I-adic filtration to show every class is represented by modules annihilated by I, giving surjectivity (proof lines 4062-4086).
Define the inverse by the graded pieces of the filtration (proof lines 4086-4092).
Check additivity through the double filtration and the exact sequences, concluding the isomorphism (proof lines 4100-4125).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a closed subscheme Z of a locally Noetherian scheme X, the exact inclusion of the category of coherent sheaves on Z into the Serre subcategory of coherent sheaves on X whose set-theoretic support lies in Z induces an isomorphism on K_0 (statement lines 4049-4060, tag 0FDT). The proof constructs the inverse map explicitly by taking the graded pieces of the I-adic filtration of a module supported on Z, and then has to prove its additivity on short exact sequences, which it does by introducing a double filtration F^{p,q} = I^p F intersect I^q G and comparing three different ways of writing the same class. The double-filtration comparison is the substance, so the claim is H2.
